title: The Fear of God and the Deception of the Devil
english: “Jerusalem,” that is, the fallen things of such a soul, is evident from the expression of Origen. Regarding the gates of the mighty, he speaks of the virtues of the wise: “For open to me, he says, the gates of righteousness” (Psalm 5:11), and “The mighty are hot-tempered; let them not drink wine, lest having drunk, they fail to perceive wisdom and be unable to judge rightly for the weak” (Proverbs 23:20). 13 1, 26 Indeed, I too shall laugh at your ruin; and I shall rejoice whenever destruction comes to you. How then does Solomon say before [the event]: “But he who rejoices at the destruction of another shall not be acquitted” (Proverbs 28:22)? Or perhaps wisdom rejoices in this way, just as she rejoiced at the loss of Matthew the tax collector and at the loss of the thief who believed in Christ. For wisdom lost the thief, but lost the tax collector. 14 1, 27.1–3 And just as an unexpected noise will reach you, so destruction will come like a storm when tribulation and siege come to you. A siege is an ethical teaching that overturns a soul badly constructed. 15 1, 30.1 It also did not wish to pay attention to me through intentions. If it is up to us to want to pay attention to the intentions of wisdom, and not to want to pay attention, we have become masters of ourselves. Similar to this is: “If you are willing and will listen to me, you shall eat the good of the earth; but if you are not willing and will not listen to me, a sword shall strike you; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things” (Matthew 9:13; Luke 23:35). 16 1, 32.1 Because they were wronging the infants, they shall be killed. Just as infants are in the midst of the righteous and the unrighteous, so all men are in the midst of angels and demons, neither being demons nor angels, making their living until the consummation of the age. 17 1, 33 And he who hears me will dwell in hope and will rest fearlessly from every evil. The one in apatheia rests fearlessly from every evil thought. 18 2, 1 Son, if having received the word of my commandment you hide it within yourself, 2, 2.1 your ear will obey wisdom. This one who does the commandment of God hides it, even though it is said that the demons snatch us away because they do not forgive it. 19 2, 3.1–2 For if you call upon wisdom and give your voice to understanding, now he calls the apatheia of the soul a 'voice'; for this is accustomed to call upon the knowledge of God. So also David says: “With my voice I cried out to the Lord” (Psalm 142:1).

And again: 'Give heed to the voice of my prayer.' Then you will realize fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God. At that time you will realize how the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom and how the knowledge of God becomes a guest. Wisdom and understanding must pre-exist so that one may be able to understand the fear of the Lord. And we shall add these things to those who despise wisdom and understanding, but who wish to flee toward fearing God as if it were an easy thing.

Then you will realize righteousness and judgment, and you will straighten all righteous axes. 'Axes' refers to the commandments of God which lead us toward the knowledge of God. And David says: 'For this reason I have kept all your commandments' (Ps 119:27). In order to be rescued from an evil way and from a man speaking nothing trustworthy. The holy angels speak all things trustworthily; men speak some things trustworthily and some things untrustworthily; but the devil speaks nothing trustworthily, rather he is not worthy of faith. For he calls the devil a 'man' now, if he is a wicked man who has sown discord.

'Son, let not an evil counsel seize you, having forgotten the teaching of youth and the divine covenant.' If counsel is a movement of the mind, how did this leave behind the teaching of youth? And how did it also overtake the divine covenant? For it discourses to us about him as if he were a rational animal. Either he calls the devil a 'bad counsel' now. For he counseled wickedly, saying, 'I will set my throne above the stars; I will be like the Most High' (Isa 14:13). And he also overtook the divine knowledge, leaving behind the teaching of youth, which youth reveals his former state, by which he was also a zealot among the trees of paradise.

All those who walk in it will not turn back, nor will they find paths of straightness; for they are not overtaken by the years of life. 'For those pursuing righteousness love' (Ps 34:14) and 'so run that you may attain' (1 Cor 9:24). Those who 'are overtaken by the years of life' are those who seize paths of straightness. And 'your mercy, he says, shall pursue me all the days of my life' (Ps 23:6). The good shall be inhabitants of the earth; but the harmless shall be left in it. Those who, he says, remained in harmlessness, were left in the land, that is, in knowledge; the...

title: Analogies of Rational Nature and Moral Virtues
english: But those having fallen through wickedness will return again through kindness. 'My son, do not forget my commandments; let your heart keep my words' (Prov 3:1). If this one forgets the law, the one not living according to it, this one remembers the law; but if this one keeps the words of God, the one doing them, this one destroys them, the one not willing to do them; 'for the hearers of the law are not righteous before God, he says, but the doers of the law will be justified' (Rom 2:13). 'Be of good trust with all your heart in God; but do not be proud of your own wisdom' (Prov 3:5-7). 'Do not be puffed up,' he says, 'having acquired the wisdom of God.' Because he says here the wisdom of God and not the human [wisdom], by which he demonstrates: 'for in all your ways you will know her, so that she may make your paths straight' (Prov 3:6).

'Then there will be healing to your body and care to your bones' (Prov 3:8). When the powers of the soul receive care, they will say the greatest things: 'Lord, who is like you? For all, he says, my bones will say: Lord, Lord, who is like you?' Because the mnemonic power of the soul, receiving care, will certainly say, 'I remembered God and was glad.' Similarly, the optic [power] will say, 'I understood your works and was astonished.' Likewise also the desiring [power]: 'Lord, all my desire is against you.' And the calculating [power] will also say, 'I considered the days of old.' According to these things, it will happen also to the other powers.

Something more precious than costly stones is; nothing evil opposes it. Toward wisdom alone, the demons are unable to cast thoughts into the heart of the one having become wise, if they are not permitted; for the mind, being occupied with the theorems of wisdom, becomes unfit for unclean thoughts. A pure mind approaches wisdom; but the unclean will be distanced from it. It is a tree of life to all those holding fast to it. Adam is prevented from partaking of this tree after the transgression, if 'a tree of life grows from the fruits of righteousness.' But if the tree of life is the wisdom of God, he is justly prevented from grasping this tree; 'for into a craftless soul, he says, wisdom will not enter.' God established [the world] by wisdom.

The earth: and the holy Paul named the breadth there; and the heavens being called height in his epistle to the Ephesians; and the so-called tropical abysses he names depth; and the cloud-formed mists he calls length. All these are symbols of rational natures, divided by worlds and bodies according to the analogy of their state.

‘That your soul may live, and that there may be grace around your neck’ (Prov 3:2, 20): ‘Neck’ he says of the soul that has borne the yoke of the Lord. ‘That all your ways may go in confidence in peace, and that your foot may not stumble’ (Prov 3:2, 23): ‘Stumbling block’ is an impure thought of rational nature or a false knowledge. ‘If you sit, you shall be without fear; and if you sleep, you shall sleep sweetly, and you shall not be afraid of a falling terror or the coming of the impulses of the ungodly’ (Prov 3:2, 24-25). From this we know that almsgiving removes fearful fantasies occurring to us in the night. Gentleness, lack of anger, and patience also do the same, restraining the passion that is prone to be disturbed, if indeed fearful phantoms are wont to arise from the disturbance of the passion.

‘Do not envy a man without cause, lest he work evil against you’ (Prov 23:17): This enmity toward the neighbor works some evil. ‘The curse of God in the houses of the ungodly; but the dwellings of the righteous are blessed’ (Prov 14:11): ‘The ignorance of the Lord in the souls of the ungodly; but the knowledge of God in the souls of the righteous’ (Prov 14:12). ‘The Lord resists the proud, but gives grace to the lowly’ (Prov 3:34): Just as the Lord resists the unrighteous as righteousness, and the liars as truth, so also he resists the proud as humility. ‘The wise shall inherit glory; but the ungodly have exalted dishonor’ (Prov 3:35): The wise shall inherit knowledge; but the ungodly have honored ignorance.

‘For I will give you a good gift’ (Prov 2:3): It should be noted here that he names the law a ‘good gift’ because the one receiving gifts in his lap unjustly is not being guided straight. For there, the commands of the evil one are called unjust gifts, which the mind receiving them is not guided straight in its ways. ‘Do not abandon my law’ (Prov 2:2): He who transgresses it abandons the law.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Exegesis of Proverbs
english: Engrave her, and she will exalt you. If it is within our power to engrave wisdom, and the virtues are within our power, then the engravings here signify the virtues which exalt the knowledge of God.

That you may give a crown of graces to your head, and a crown of splendor may protect you; the knowledge of God is a crown of grace and a crown of splendor, which also protects us from every passionate thought and every rejected false knowledge.

Listen, son, and receive my words, and the years of your life shall be multiplied, so that many paths of life may become yours. These many paths lead into one path which said, 'I am the way' (John 14:6). The virtues have spoken of many paths that lead to the knowledge of Christ.
In whatever place they may encamp, do not go there; but turn away from them and deviate. The place of this army is wickedness and false knowledge.

For they shall never sleep unless they do evil; sleep is taken away from them, they do not sleep. If the Lord gives sleep to his beloved, the impious are not his beloved; the Lord does not give sleep to the impious. From this it is also possible to show that the demons are not even able to sleep.

For these feed on the grain of impiety; and they get drunk on lawless wine. From this we know what the army of the opposing power is nourished by; for, he says, the grain is impiety and the wine is lawlessness.

But the paths of the righteous shine similarly with light; they go forward and illuminate, until the day is perfected. Our virtues go forward and illuminate us, until the sun of righteousness shines his own day upon us.

But the paths of the impious are dark; they do not know how they stumble. The impious do not even know the way in which they sin, nor do they know the cause from where they stumble, but they do not even know this, that they act lawlessly, which is the mark of ultimate folly.

So that your springs may not fail you, guard them in your heart. He calls the virtues 'springs,' from which the living water is generated, which is the knowledge of Christ. And David says: 'The springs of the waters appeared' (Psalm 114:15).
The foundations of the world were revealed, through the manifestation of our Savior Christ.
Let your eyes see uprightly; and let your eyelids be righteous. Those who have dispassionate thoughts and true doctrines, these see uprightly.

Do not turn to the right nor to the left; but turn your foot from the evil way. For virtue is a mean; therefore they say that courage is between rashness and cowardice. Now, 'right' names not those which are naturally right, but those things which appear to be right because of pleasures; 'for the north, he says, is a harsh wind; but it is called skillful by name.' Saying 'north' symbolically refers to the evil one, from whom all evils were burned upon the earth.
He himself will make your paths straight; and he will lead your journey in peace. This agrees with 'unless the Lord builds a house' (Psalm 127:1) and 'keeps a city' (Psalm 127:1) and so on.

Do not pay attention to a bad woman; for honey turns away from the lips of a prostitute, who for a time moistens your throat, but later you will find it more bitter than bile and more piercing than a double-edged sword. Fat signifies pleasure, from which impurity is brought forth, from which wickedness and ignorance are born, of which nothing more bitter is found among existing things.
For the feet of those using folly descend after death into Hades. She who was above, the prostitute, now named folly.

David prays for those descending after death into Hades, saying, 'Let the living descend into Hades' (Psalm 88:4). For the ways of life do not arrive; but its paths are unstable and not well-known. If the paths are not well-known, it has been well said, 'they do not know how they stumble' (Psalm 119:176).
Make your road long from it; do not approach the doors of her houses. Here he spoke of the mind walking toward virtue. Perhaps virtue protects us by separating us from wickedness.
So that others may not take your life and have mercy on your life. From this we know that the irascible part prevails in the wicked; 'for an irascible spirit, he says, and sharp anger' (Psalm 129:2).
Whenever the flesh of your body is worn away by evils, the wicked [through evils]...
